title: Hybrid capture coordinator and spectator replay mode for multi-stream decodes
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a hybrid capture coordinator and a 'spectator' replay execution mode to improve capture stability and replay correctness for concurrent multi-stream decodes. The coordinator serializes capture-critical sections while allowing non-critical kernels to run lock-free. Spectator replay runs a shadow replay path to validate kernel bindings, buffer lifetimes, and KV cache state without affecting the live decode path. The goal is to reduce nondeterministic recapture failures, lower tail latency spikes caused by unexpected recaptures, and provide deterministic signals for automated rollback/fallback policies.
technical_background: We see recurrent nondeterministic failures in CUDA Graph capture/replay when multiple streams with interleaved prefill/decode patterns interact: kernel affinity oscillation, KV cache epoch mismatch, and partially-captured stochastic kernels. Prior tickets addressed capture segmentation and fence protocol but we still observe rare divergence during replay after preemption or stream bumping. Current instrumentation lacks a lightweight on-host verification mode to detect binding/state drift before it impacts production.
decisions: 1) Introduce a coordinator that only serializes graph-capture-critical sections (kernel binding negotiation, KV-epoch advance, and prefill endpoint sealing) rather than full-stream locks. 2) Add a 'spectator' replay mode: create a shadow CUDA Graph replay executed on a disabled-affinity stream to validate replay determinism; it can be run synchronously during rollout and asynchronously as sampling in steady-state. 3) Use lightweight replay fingerprints (checksum of select intermediate tensors + kernel invocation sequence) to detect drift instead of full-buffer comparisons.
tradeoffs:
- Serializing only critical sections minimizes throughput loss but increases implementation complexity.
- Spectator mode increases GPU work (shadow replays) or host compute if executed on CPU; we will sample at low rates (1-5%) to limit cost.
- Fingerprinting reduces data movement but can produce false positives if we don't choose robust invariants; we bias towards kernel sequence + KV-key hashes to lower false alarms.
implementation_steps: Design coordinator API and critical section boundaries (kernel-negotiation, prefill-seal, kv-epoch-advance)
Add capture-fingerprint generator to CUDA-graph runtime (sequence IDs + small tensor checksums)
Implement spectator replay executor that runs shadow replays at configurable sampling rates
Integrate a divergence detector that logs events, triggers tracing, and optionally flags the request for fallback
Add metrics: spectator_replays_total, spectator_replay_mismatches, coordinator_wait_ns, capture_recapture_rate
Create a toggle in runtime config for 'spectator_mode_sampling' and 'coordinator_strictness'
Wire up a safe fallback policy: on mismatch threshold -> immediate per-node fallback to eager decode + trigger alert and rollout pause
test_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint computation (deterministic on fixed seeds)
Integration test: multi-stream prefill/decode with synthetic traffic generator to validate zero false negatives on known-good workload
Chaos test: simulate stream preemption, delayed kernel launch, and GPU context switching; assert spectator mismatch detection and safe fallback
Perf test: 72-hour soak on staging cluster with spectator sampling at 2% to measure throughput impact (<5% p99 delta target)
A/B rollout in canary pool: 10% traffic with spectator enabled and coordinator strictness=relaxed, monitor capture_recapture_rate and error rates
rollout_strategy: Phase 1: Deploy coordinator with strictness=relaxed and spectator_mode sampling=0 (metrics only) to collect baseline. Phase 2: Enable spectator sampling at 1% on canary nodes for 48h. Phase 3: If mismatch rate < 0.1% and p99 latency impact < 3%, increase sampling to 2-5% and flip coordinator strictness to normal. Phase 4: Full rollout with monitoring alerts and automated fallback thresholds configured.
metrics_and_sla_goals:
- Reduce recapture-triggered tail spikes by >= 50% vs baseline.
- spectator_replay_mismatches <= 0.1% at 1% sampling (indicator of divergence rate).
- coordinator_wait_ns median increase < 500ns; p95 < 2ms.
- end-to-end p99 latency regression < 3% on steady-state traffic at sampling=2%.
observability_plan: Emit structured events on mismatch with capture fingerprint, kernel sequence id, active stream ids, and KV epoch. Hook into Console trace collector and add a per-run dashboard showing mismatch rate, coordinator contention, and recapture events. Link alerts to runbook for rollback and to PRs/CLs for postmortem tracking.
